const answer = `IDEA: LCB-RQ
TITLE: Lorentz co-consumption barycentre targets inside a curved-residual RQ-VAE
MOTIVATION: Behaviourally co-consumed items (same session, close positions) currently get unrelated SIDs because Stage-2 only reconstructs an item's own text embedding; nothing in the objective asks two items that co-occur to share a prefix. The probe numbers of the plain Euclidean RQ-VAE (Spearman 0.0402, top-10 overlap 0.0124) show the code space is behaviour-blind. This proposal moves the quantization target itself along a geodesic toward a behaviour anchor, so co-consumed items are quantized from nearly the same point and must share codes.
NOVELTY: Earlier mechanisms here acted on the codebook update (successor-weighted Frechet means), on per-level curvature from prefix-transition scores, on radial position from context entropy, on cones, on mixed-curvature fibres and on recursive graph cuts. None of them moves the item-side quantization target. LCB-RQ changes what is fed to the quantizer: each item's Lorentzian target is a geodesic barycentre between its own text point and the Lorentz Frechet mean of its co-consumed neighbours' text points, and the whole residual chain then runs in the curved space, so curvature re-shapes level-2 and level-3 residuals rather than only a distance.
CHANGE: Precompute, once from the training split, a symmetric popularity-adjusted co-consumption graph and a per-item Lorentz barycentre of neighbours' text points; during Stage-2 replace each item's quantization point by the geodesic blend of its own text point and that anchor, with the blend weight fixed by measured co-consumption mass, and replace the Euclidean residual recursion by Lorentz exp/log residual quantization with a trainable curvature.
SPECIFICATION: See SPEC EQUATIONS. In one line: t_i = exp^K_{x_i}( a_i * log^K_{x_i}( b_i ) ), b_i = Frechet_K({x_j : j in N(i)}, pi_ij), a_i = m_i/(m_i + median(m)), and the RQ chain is r_1 = log^K_{c_1}(z), r_{l+1} = log^K_{c_{l+1}}( exp^K_{c_l}(r_l) transported ), all distances d_K.
COST: Anchor construction is a one-off pass over 24556 items x at most 20 neighbours x 3 fixed-point iterations of exp/log, roughly 1.5M exp/log evaluations, seconds on one GPU, done once before epoch 1 and frozen. Per training step the extra work is B x L exp/log pairs for the curved residual chain (B = batch, L = 3 levels, about 1.5k-6k exp/log per step) plus one 0.5B x 0.5B? no: plus one Lorentz distance matrix B x K per level. At the frozen scale (24 steps/epoch x 3000 epochs = 72000 steps) this is about 1.1e8-4.3e8 extra exp/log evaluations in total, roughly 3-6 percent wall-clock over the baseline Stage-2 and zero extra epochs; Stage-3, the decoder forward pass and the sequence model are untouched.
HYPOTHESIS: If behaviour-coherent quantization targets are what the SID is missing, then co-consumed items must land in the same or adjacent codes, so the two probe numbers should both rise well above 0.0402 and 0.0124 (target at least 0.10 / 0.05) and the learned curvature should stay bounded away from 0, which is observable as a non-degenerate K and as a shrinking mean geodesic pull distance ||log^K_{x_i}(t_i)|| over epochs; only then is a Stage-3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 plausible, and that number is reported with the explicit single-run caveat of about 0.013 noise.
RISKS: Over-pulling collapses many items onto one prefix, which raises raw overlap but flattens the code-distance distribution and can lower Spearman and destroy reconstruction, so the weight must be mass-derived and the target clamped inside a radius shell. Curvature may drift to 0, making the geometry arm identical to the Euclidean one; the softplus parameterisation plus an initialization at K = 1 and a lower clamp at 1e-3 guards this but does not prove it. Items with no co-consumption get a_i = 0 and behave exactly like the baseline, so a sparse training split would make the whole mechanism a no-op on most items. Reconstruction of the original text embedding is no longer directly optimised for pulled items, which can hurt Stage-3 if the generator relies on literal text content; a possible symptom is a good probe and a flat or worse recall.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Symmetric, windowed session co-consumption with popularity adjustment, i.e. an undirected version of the transition signal rather than the directed successor counts used by the earlier rounds.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the training split only, scan every user session; for every pair of item positions (p, q) with 0 < |p - q| <= 5 in the same session add 1 to c_ij. Set pop_i = sum_j c_ij, define w_ij = c_ij / ( sqrt(pop_i * pop_j) + 1 ), keep the top 20 neighbours per item by w_ij, symmetrise by max, row-normalise to pi_ij, and store the sparse list once before Stage-2. The 5 and the 20 are documented defaults of the graph construction, not tuned constants of the loss.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: The co-consumption counts are read only from the training split sequences; validation and test interactions are never touched, and the resulting anchor table is computed once before epoch 1 and frozen, so no validation or test signal can enter the SID construction. The probe and Stage-3 read the frozen SIDs afterwards and never feed back.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: The Lorentz hyperboloid L^D_K with trainable positive curvature K = softplus(theta) + 1e-3, initialized so that K = 1; Minkowski inner product <x,y>_L = -x_0 y_0 + x.y; d_K(x,y) = (1/sqrt(K)) * arcosh(-K <x,y>_L); exp^K_o and log^K_o at the origin o = (1/sqrt(K), 0, ..., 0); Lorentz Frechet mean by three tangent-space fixed-point iterations; and geodesic residual quantization, in which each RQ level encodes a tangent vector at the previously chosen code.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Three places in Stage-2, all tied to the same K: (i) construction of the per-item quantization target (geodesic blend and Frechet anchor), (ii) the RQ assignment and commitment term, which use d_K instead of squared Euclidean distance, (iii) the residual chain, where level l+1 quantizes exp^K_{c_l}(r_l) after parallel transport of r_l from c_l to the origin frame instead of the vector difference z - sum q.

Setting the behaviour term to zero gives t_i = x_i and the curved RQ still runs; setting K to 0 (Euclidean limit) removes the geodesic blend and the curved residuals and leaves a plain behaviour-smoothed Euclidean RQ-VAE. Both switches therefore change the same tensor that the quantizer consumes.
COUPLING EQUATION: t_i = exp^K_{x_i}( a_i * log^K_{x_i}( b_i ) ), with b_i = argmin_b sum_j pi_ij * d_K(b, x_j)^2 and a_i = m_i / (m_i + m_ref), m_ref = median_i(m_i), m_i = sum_j w_ij, and the level-l quantizer minimizing d_K( exp^K_{c_l}(r_l), c_l ) subject to the transport rule r_{l+1} = PT_{c_l -> o} log^K_{c_l}( exp^K_{c_l}(r_l) ) - handled as in SPEC EQUATIONS.
OBSERVABLES: The exact probe of this round: Spearman between code-space distance and d_beh = -log((n_ij+1)/(sqrt(pop_i pop_j)+1)), and top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap, both before (0.0402 / 0.0124) and after; the learned K; the mean geodesic pull ||log^K_{x_i}(t_i)|| per epoch; code-usage entropy and prefix counts (recorded, not gating); and Stage-3 test_recall@10 with the roughly 0.013 single-run caveat.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: a_i := 0 for every item, so t_i = x_i and the anchors are never used; the curved residual quantizer, the trainable K and all other code paths are unchanged. This run must reproduce the geometry-only behaviour, and the code exists but is not trained in this round.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: K -> 0, i.e. arcosh replaced by the Euclidean limit, exp/log replaced by identity, Frechet mean replaced by the arithmetic mean of neighbour embeddings and the residual chain replaced by z - sum q, while pi_ij, m_i and a_i stay active; this is a behaviour-smoothed plain Euclidean RQ-VAE.
ABLATION BOTH ON: the full LCB-RQ as specified, trained once for 3000 Stage-2 epochs on four cards with the frozen Stage-3 protocol of 150 epochs, no early stopping, no sweep, no second seed.
SPEC EQUATIONS:
  graph: c_ij from window-5 session co-occurrence on train; w_ij = c_ij/(sqrt(pop_i pop_j)+1); pi_ij = w_ij / sum_k w_ik; m_i = sum_j w_ij; a_i = m_i/(m_i+median(m)).
  lift: x_i = exp^K_o( [0, e_i / ||e_i||] ) with e_i the frozen text embedding, tangent scale fixed at 1.
  anchor: b_i^(0) = exp^K_o( sum_j pi_ij log^K_o(x_j) ); repeat 3 times b_i^(t+1) = exp^K_{b_i^(t)}( sum_j pi_ij log^K_{b_i^(t)}(x_j) ).
  target: t_i = exp^K_{x_i}( a_i * log^K_{x_i}( b_i ) ), then clamp with t_i <- exp^K_o( min(1, R/||log^K_o(t_i)||) * log^K_o(t_i) ), R = 99th percentile of ||log^K_o(x_i)||.
  encode: u_i = log^K_o(t_i) (D-dim tangent vector); z = E(u_i) in the tangent space at o, mapped in as Z_i = exp^K_o(z).
  level 1: k_1 = argmin_k d_K(Z_i, c_1k); r_1 = log^K_{c_1 k_1}(Z_i).
  level l+1 (l = 1..L-1): v_l = PT_{c_l -> o}(r_l) computed as log^K_o( exp^K_{c_l}( r_l ) ), point p_l = exp^K_o( v_l ), k_{l+1} = argmin_k d_K(p_l, c_{l+1,k}), r_{l+1} = log^K_{c_{l+1}k}( p_l ).
  loss: sum_l [ d_K( sg(p_l), c_{l,k} )^2 + beta * d_K( p_l, sg(c_{l,k}) )^2 ] + || dec( log^K_o( exp^K_o( sum_l ... ) ) ) - e_i ||^2 in the Euclidean tangent with the baseline MSE, beta kept at the baseline default.
  steering: only the target t_i and the residual geometry change; the optimizer, schedule, batch size and epoch count are the frozen ones.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: frozen text embeddings e_i for 24556 items, the sparse co-consumption table (top 20 per item, pi and m), the curvature parameter theta, the L codebooks. Output: a per-item Lorentz target t_i (and its tangent vector u_i), a per-step curved RQ forward pass returning the level codes k_1..k_L, the transported residuals and the curved commitment/reconstruction loss; the emitted SID is the code tuple, unchanged in format from the baseline.
SAFEGUARDS: clamp the arcosh argument to at least 1 + 1e-7 and at most 1e12; enforce the hyperboloid constraint by re-projecting every point with x <- x / sqrt(-K <x,x>_L) after each update; clamp tangent norms to R_max = 1.05 * R to stop boundary blow-up; clamp K into [1e-3, 10] with softplus so the Euclidean limit is reachable but never reached; use float64 for the anchor precompute and float32 for training; if an item has m_i = 0 set a_i = 0 and skip it in the anchor loop; guard the parallel transport with a norm floor of 1e-8; log the fraction of items with a_i > 0 and abort the coupling (set a := 0) only if that fraction is below 0.5 as a data check, decided before training and not a tuned constant.

TITLE: Lorentz co-consumption barycentre targets inside a curved-residual RQ-VAE
